title: Experimental demonstration of entanglement sudden death induced by natural dissipation
authors: Yan Wang, Hao-Long Zhang, Jia-Hao Lü, Ken Chen, Wen Ning, Li-Hua Lin, Zhen-Biao Yang, Shi-Biao Zheng
abstract: Any quantum system inevitably interacts with its natural environment, which can be modeled as a Markovian reservoir consisting of a continuum of electromagnetic field modes. The quantum coherence of qubits in a zero-temperature natural reservoir decays asymptotically, whereas the quantum entanglement of two qubits coupled to such reservoirs may disappear in a finite time. This phenomenon, referred to as entanglement sudden death (ESD), has been simulated with artificially engineered dissipative channels, but ESD induced by natural dissipative channels has not been confirmed. We here present the first demonstration of natural-dissipation-induced ESD for two photonic qubits, each stored in a leaky resonator of a superconducting circuit. The disentanglement dynamics of the two photonic qubits is monitored with two ancilla superconducting qubits, which can be controllably coupled to the corresponding leaky resonators. The techniques developed in our experiment pave the way for experimental exploration of entanglement dynamics in natural environments.
summary: The authors experimentally demonstrated Entanglement Sudden Death (ESD) for two photonic qubits using superconducting circuit resonators. By monitoring entanglement decay under natural dissipation from leaky environments, they confirmed that entanglement can vanish in finite time even when the underlying photon loss is asymptotic. This work validates a key theoretical prediction regarding decoherence in realistic quantum hardware.
main_problem: The primary goal was to experimentally demonstrate Entanglement Sudden Death (ESD) induced by natural environmental dissipation in a quantum system.
main_result: The experiment successfully demonstrated that the entanglement between two photonic qubits decays completely to zero within a finite time due to coupling with natural leaky resonators, confirming ESD.
method: The researchers used a circuit QED platform involving superconducting qubits and leaky microwave resonators to prepare entangled states and monitor their decay dynamics.
model_or_system: The system consists of two photonic qubits stored in leaky resonators coupled to superconducting circuits. The evolution is governed by a Lindblad master equation, modeling interaction with a Markovian reservoir.
key_observables: Concurrence ($C$), which quantifies entanglement; density matrix elements ($ho_{10,10}, ho_{01,01}$); and the time-dependent decay of these quantities.
important_parameters: Photonic decay rates ($\kappa_1, \kappa_2$); resonator frequencies ($\omega_{r1}, \omega_{r2}$); and the initial entanglement strength parameter ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Born-Markov approximation for modeling environmental coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the setup, pulse sequences, measured concurrence decay showing a sudden drop to zero (ESD), and time evolution plots of density matrix elements.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical setup using superconducting circuits, describes state preparation via controlled coupling, models the dynamics using master equations, measures entanglement decay over time, and compares results against theoretical predictions for ESD.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial experimental confirmation of a non-trivial quantum phenomenon (ESD) in a realistic, naturally dissipative environment, advancing the field of open quantum systems beyond idealized artificial channels.
